main.title: Life Is Strange: True Colors
main.subtitle: Feeling What Others Feel Does Not Mean Deciding for Them
main.summary: On September 10, 2021, Deck Nine released Life Is Strange: True Colors on PlayStation, Xbox, Windows and Stadia, published by Square Enix.

cards.heading: Feeling What Others Feel Does Not Mean Deciding for Them
cards.text: Deck Nine and Square Enix released Life Is Strange: True Colors on PlayStation, Xbox, Windows and Stadia on September 10, 2021. The complete season arrived at once. Alex Chen comes to Haven Springs, a Colorado mining town, with a power that makes intense emotions perceptible. Returning to its streets and residents develops both her relationships and the mystery she is investigating.

cards.heading: An Emotion Changes the Space Around It
cards.text: Alex perceives strong emotions through colour, movement, sound and changes to the environment. Sadness uses cool tones, fear brings pulses and sharp forms, anger intensifies image and breathing, and joy adds warmth and light. Emotional novas reveal another person's perception, giving Alex information that conversation alone might miss. Acting on that knowledge becomes part of the player's choices.

cards.heading: A Small Town Becomes Shared Memory
cards.text: The record shop, bar, park and streets recur throughout the story. Exploring their side paths and businesses lets Alex meet residents beyond the needs of the main investigation. Returning to a place brings earlier conversations into context as relationships and tensions change. Familiarity with Haven Springs grows through both its layout and the people occupying it.

cards.heading: Alex's Voice Also Passes Through Songs
cards.text: Music appears in shops, headphones, broadcasts and performances. The soundtrack combines original work by Angus & Julia Stone, mxmtoon and Novo Amor with licensed songs including Radiohead and Phoebe Bridgers. Alex also sings and plays guitar, expressing feelings she may find harder to discuss. Listening and performing become part of her daily life in the town.

main.title: Deathloop
main.summary: Deathloop is a 2021 first-person shooter game developed by Arkane Lyon and published by Bethesda Softworks.

cards.heading: Eight targets in one repeating day
cards.text: Deathloop is a 2021 first-person shooter game developed by Arkane Lyon and published by Bethesda Softworks. The player controls Colt Vahn, an assassin who must escape a time loop by killing eight targets known as visionaries before midnight each day. The story is set on an island named Blackreef. Each day is divided into morning, noon, afternoon, and evening; and moving between the island's four districts causes time to advance. Using Colt's arsenal of gear and powers, the player must identify the optimal way to kill all targets in one day. As with Arkane's previous games, Deathloop is an immersive sim, with the game providing players a variety of ways to approach their objectives.

cards.heading: An island built for experimentation
cards.text: Development of Deathloop began in 2018, originally as a smaller-scale project that allowed Arkane to experiment with new gameplay mechanics. The game was built on Arkane's previous works, such as Dishonored, introducing nonlinear gameplay and removing the morality system, enabling players to take risks without considering narrative repercussions, as well as Prey: Mooncrash, which experimented with the roguelike formula and remix gameplay using a limited amount of assets. Arkane implemented asymmetrical multiplayer, an unused gameplay mechanic from its unreleased game The Crossing that enables a second player to control Julianna and hunt Colt. Films and television series like Groundhog Day and The Avengers inspired the story and aesthetics, while the Scottish Highlands and the Faroe Islands inspired the design of Blackreef.

cards.heading: Release, reception and a shared universe
cards.text: Deathloop was released on 14 September 2021 for Windows PC and PlayStation 5, and for Xbox Series X and Series S on 20 September 2022. Although the story takes place in the Dishonored universe, Bethesda did not market it as a spin-off of that franchise because it has a distinct story and characters. Deathloop received generally positive reviews; critics praised its gameplay, structure, art direction, characters and story, but criticized its artificial intelligence. Many critics described Deathloop as original and regarded it as one of Arkane Studio's best games. By February 2023 it had attracted more than five million players, and it was nominated for several end-of-year accolades, including Game of the Year at the Game Awards, D.I.C.E. Awards, and British Academy Games Awards.

main.title: Kazuko Shibuya
main.subtitle: 2021: Pixel Remaster and a retrospective on her pixel art
main.summary: What does remaking early Final Fantasy pixel art reveal about its original making?

cards.heading: A printout becomes a working record
cards.text: Kazuko Shibuya redrew the first Final Fantasy's prologue landscape as silhouettes to fit limited memory. It appeared when the player crossed the bridge. Recreating that scene for Pixel Remaster years later required another kind of reference: the original digital data was unavailable, but she had kept a printout. The paper copy helped her return to the released image and its earlier design decisions.

cards.heading: A pixel changes with its screen
cards.text: Shibuya described how neighbouring colours behaved on cathode-ray-tube displays, producing relationships different from sharply separated modern pixels. Redrawing an early sprite therefore involved considering the screen for which it had been made. A remaster could retain the character's appeal while changing how those colours and edges were presented.

cards.heading: The sprite was shared work
cards.text: Koichi Ishii recalled working with Shibuya and Takashi Tokita on the first Final Fantasy. While Shibuya was occupied elsewhere, Tokita taught him the sprite tools, and Ishii developed the side-view battle presentation. Character design, learning the tools and entering the images into the game involved several contributors.

cards.heading: A remaster names the kind of change
cards.text: Square Enix's Pixel Remaster FAQ credits Shibuya with redrawn character graphics intended to preserve the earlier games' feel. It separately identifies illustration galleries and Yoshitaka Amano's concept art. The project brings those related forms of artwork together, while new sprites adapt the original character designs for another presentation.

main.title: Far Cry 6
main.summary: Far Cry 6 is a 2021 open world first-person shooter game developed by Ubisoft Toronto and published by Ubisoft.

cards.heading: Dani Rojas and the fight for Yara
cards.text: Far Cry 6 is a 2021 open world first-person shooter game developed by Ubisoft Toronto and published by Ubisoft. It is the sixth main installment in the Far Cry series and the successor to 2018's Far Cry 5. The game is set on the fictional Caribbean island of Yara, ruled as a dictatorship by "El Presidente" Antón Castillo (portrayed by Giancarlo Esposito), who is raising his son Diego (Anthony Gonzalez) to follow in his rule. Players take on the role of guerrilla fighter Dani Rojas (voiced by either Nisa Gunduz or Sean Rey), attempting to topple Castillo and his regime. Gameplay focuses on combat and exploration; players battle enemy soldiers and dangerous wildlife using a wide array of weapons and gadgets. The game features numerous elements commonly found in role-playing games, such as a leveling-up system and side quests. It also features a cooperative multiplayer mode.

cards.heading: An island to explore and fight across
cards.text: Similar to the previous entries in the series, Far Cry 6 is a first-person shooter game, set in an open world environment navigable on foot or via various land, water, and air vehicles. Players assume the role of a local rebel named Dani Rojas, a former conscript in the military turned into a guerrilla fighter, whose gender they can select at the start of the game. The world is divided into seven main regions with an array of terrain, ranging from urban areas and dense jungles, to mountain ranges and open oceans. Gameplay focuses on armed and close-quarters combat. Players are able to use a wide array of conventional weapons (such as sidearms, assault rifles, submachine guns, shotguns, light-machine guns, sniper rifles and grenade launchers). Firearms can be customized using materials found throughout the world.

cards.heading: Resolver weapons and Supremo backpacks
cards.text: In a new addition to the series, the game features several prototypes of special weaponry, called "Resolver weapons", each offering a certain perk to the player's loadout, for example a silent close-range nailgun or a sling-shot projectile weapon which fires CDs. Another new addition is the "Supremo" backpacks, allowing augmentation of the playstyle by assigning more perks to the player's loadout, such as firing homing missiles or seeing enemies through solid objects. Unlike the previous titles in the series, players are able to holster weapons; as a result, enemy NPCs will not attack the player on sight, unless within restricted areas.

cards.heading: Guerrilla camps and animal companions
cards.text: The player has the ability to construct and upgrade guerrilla bases called "Camp Facilities", which provide useful resources and in-game bonuses to increase the skillset of the character, specialize perks in hunting animals, unlock fast travel locations throughout Yara, enlist new recruits and manage their equipment, or launch friendly NPC operations. The game's version of Far Cry 5's "Fangs for Hire" companion system returns, called "Amigos", which features recruitable animals with a variety of abilities and perks tasked to assist the player in combat and exploration.

main.title: Metroid Dread
main.summary: Metroid Dread is a 2021 action-adventure game developed by MercurySteam and Nintendo EPD and published by Nintendo for the Nintendo Switch.

cards.heading: Metroid Dread
cards.text: Metroid Dread is a 2021 action-adventure game developed by MercurySteam and Nintendo EPD and published by Nintendo for the Nintendo Switch. Released on October 8, 2021, Dread is the fifth game in the 2D Metroid series and a sequel to Metroid Fusion (2002). It retains the side-scrolling gameplay of previous Metroid games and incorporates stealth elements. Players control the bounty hunter Samus Aran as she investigates the source of a mysterious transmission on the planet ZDR.

cards.heading: Making the game
cards.text: The Metroid producer, Yoshio Sakamoto, conceived Dread for the Nintendo DS in the mid-2000s, but development ended due to technical limitations. Industry commentators expressed interest in a new 2D Metroid game, and listed Dread in their "most wanted" lists. After their work on Metroid: Samus Returns (2017), Sakamoto appointed MercurySteam to develop Dread. It was announced at E3 2021.

cards.heading: Reception and legacy
cards.text: Metroid Dread was named one of the best games of 2021 by multiple outlets. At the Game Awards 2021, it received two nominations, including Game of the Year and winning for Best Action/Adventure Game. It became the fastest-selling Metroid game in Japan, the UK and the US, and has sold more than three million copies, making it the best-selling Metroid game. A sequel, Metroid Ravenous, is scheduled for 2027 for the Nintendo Switch 2.

main.title: Poppy Playtime
main.summary: Poppy Playtime is an episodic puzzle survival horror video game series first developed and published in October 2021 by American indie developer Mob Entertainment.

cards.heading: Returning to the toy factory
cards.text: Poppy Playtime is an episodic puzzle survival horror video game series first developed and published in October 2021 by American indie developer Mob Entertainment. The game is set in an abandoned factory owned by the fictional toy company Playtime Co. The player controls a former employee who receives a letter inviting them back to the factory years after the company's staff disappeared without a trace.

cards.heading: A story released in chapters
cards.text: The first chapter was released for Windows on October 12, 2021, and later ported to Android and iOS on March 11, 2022, the PlayStation 4 and PlayStation 5 on December 20, 2023, the Nintendo Switch on December 25, and the Xbox One and Xbox Series X/S on July 12, 2024. The second chapter was released for Windows on May 5, 2022, and the PlayStation 4 and 5, the Xbox One and Xbox Series X/S on September 20, 2024. The third chapter was released on Windows in January 2024, and the PlayStation 4 and 5, the Xbox One and Xbox Series X/S on September 20, 2024. The fourth chapter was released on Windows on January 30, 2025. The fifth chapter released on February 18, 2026 for Windows. All chapters after the first are premium downloadable content.

cards.heading: Reception and controversies
cards.text: Poppy Playtime has garnered a positive reception for its atmosphere, story, and gameplay, although it has also been criticized for having numerous bugs. The game faced several controversies, including its aesthetics and character design's similarities to that of children-oriented media, resulting in popularity among young demographics. The announcement of in-game non-fungible token content in December 2021 received harsh criticism, resulting in the developers donating all profits from the tokens to charity.

main.title: Back 4 Blood
main.subtitle: The Cooperative Horde Returns, and Every Run Starts With a Deck
main.summary: On October 12, 2021, Back 4 Blood arrived on PlayStation 4, PlayStation 5, Xbox One, Xbox Series X|S and PC.

cards.heading: The Cooperative Horde Returns, and Every Run Starts With a Deck
cards.text: Turtle Rock Studios and Warner Bros. Games released Back 4 Blood for PlayStation, Xbox and PC on October 12, 2021. Four Cleaners cooperate against the Ridden, people transformed by the Devil Worm parasite. The studio returned to the horde-shooter format it had helped establish with Left 4 Dead, adding decks that modify characters and the conditions of a campaign.

cards.heading: A Return to the Genre Its Makers Helped Define
cards.text: Campaign chapters connect safe rooms, while special mutations threaten players who become separated. Four teammates must cover one another while progressing together. Back 4 Blood adds character progression and preparation around that shared survival, letting a group's choices before the next encounter affect its available strengths.

cards.heading: The Deck Decides Before the Horde Arrives
cards.text: At launch, players assembled decks whose cards changed health, damage, stamina and other abilities, drawing them during a run. Complementary builds could cover a team's weaknesses. Corruption cards added obstacles such as fog or larger hordes. An update on June 7, 2022 changed this system so all fifteen player-deck cards were active from the start of a campaign on every difficulty.

cards.heading: When the Horde Has Players of Its Own
cards.text: Swarm pits four Cleaners against four players controlling mutated Ridden. Teams swap roles after a round, alternating survival with coordinated attacks. Turtle Rock later expanded the game through Tunnels of Terror, Children of the Worm and River of Blood. On February 2, 2023 the studio announced that no further content would follow.

main.title: Inscryption
main.summary: Inscryption is a 2021 roguelike deck-building game developed by Daniel Mullins Games and published by Devolver Digital.

cards.heading: The cabin and the cards
cards.text: Inscryption is a 2021 roguelike deck-building game developed by Daniel Mullins Games and published by Devolver Digital. Directed by Daniel Mullins, it was originally released for Windows on October 19, 2021, and on Linux, macOS, PlayStation 4, PlayStation 5, Nintendo Switch, Xbox One and Xbox Series X/S over the following two years. The game puts the player in a cabin where a mysterious gamemaster makes them play a tabletop game.

cards.heading: Genres and clues beyond the table
cards.text: Inscryption blends various genres, including deck-building, roguelike, turn-based strategy, escape room, puzzle and adventure, while drawing inspiration from, among others, tabletop role-playing games, board games, horror, vlogs, and found footage. Its presentation is a combination of computer animation, pixel art, drawn art, and live action, as well as first person, third-person and 2.5D perspectives. It provides no context nor backstory at its start; its cryptic, metafictional narrative must be put together from subsequent story elements and various optional clues. A real-world alternate reality game (ARG), embedded both in video from the game and outside of it, offers additional story elements via many easter eggs that must be decrypted.

cards.heading: From prototype to Kaycee's Mod
cards.text: The game originated as Sacrifices Must Be Made, a much shorter and simpler game made by Mullins in 2018 for a Ludum Dare game jam, which used a deck-building system in which the player had to kill their own creatures to summon others. After publishing the prototype to itch.io in December 2018, the positive response led Mullins to significantly expand on the original game, resulting in the making of Inscryption. The game received positive reviews upon release, winning several Game of the Year awards and selling 1 million copies by January 2022: its originality, card battle system, visuals and narrative were particularly praised, although changes in the later parts of the game received some criticism.  A free expansion titled Kaycee's Mod, allowing players to focus on the tabletop game without Inscryption's various other elements, was released in March 2022.

main.title: Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy
main.summary: Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy is a 2021 action-adventure game developed by Eidos-Montréal and originally published by Square Enix.

cards.heading: Leading the Guardians
cards.text: Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy is a 2021 action-adventure game developed by Eidos-Montréal and originally published by Square Enix. Set in an original universe based on the Marvel Comics superhero team of the same name, the game's plot follows the Guardians who, while attempting to capture a beast for a wealthy collector, inadvertently trigger a catastrophe which threatens the peace of the galaxy. The player controls the team's self-proclaimed leader, Star-Lord, and issues commands to other Guardians including Drax the Destroyer, Gamora, Rocket Raccoon and Groot. At certain points in the game, the player makes key decisions via dialogue trees that affect the relationships between Guardians and change the outcome of missions.

cards.heading: A solo adventure with a collective voice
cards.text: Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy was the second game developed in partnership between Marvel Entertainment and Square Enix. The game is strictly single-player and has no downloadable content or microtransactions, marking a departure from Marvel Entertainment and Square Enix's previous game, Marvel's Avengers. Marvel collaborated closely with the team at Eidos to create an original version of the Guardians. Despite the game's lighthearted tone, themes of trauma and grief are central to the story. The soundtrack comprises an original score composed by Richard Jacques, various licensed songs from the 1970s and 1980s, and a 1980s-inspired album by the game's audio director, Steve Szczepkowski.

cards.heading: Release and reception
cards.text: Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy was announced in June 2021 and was released for PlayStation 4, PlayStation 5, Windows, Xbox One, and Xbox Series X/S on October 26, 2021. A cloud streaming version for Nintendo Switch was released on the same day. A port for Nintendo Switch 2 with exclusive content will release under the subtitle Encore Edition in November 2026. While anticipation for the game was low due to the lackluster reception of Marvel's Avengers, it received generally positive reviews from critics. It was praised for its narrative, music, characters, and cast performance, but its gameplay and combat systems drew mixed reactions. The game was nominated for several year-end accolades by gaming publications, as well as winning awards for "Best Narrative" at The Game Awards 2021, along with "Adventure Game of the Year" and "Outstanding Achievement in Story" at the 25th Annual D.I.C.E. Awards. Despite positive critical reception, the game failed to meet Square Enix's sales expectations.
